deepdive.divline: Debt reduction prioritized (repaid some promoter loans in Q4)
deepdive.netdebt: INR 138cr consolidated (INR 70cr promoter loans, INR 68cr bank term loans)

profile.entities: Sejal Glass Limited (Parent); Glasstech India (Subsidiary - Taloja & Erode units); Sejal Glass UAE
profile.subseg: Insulated Glass (IG); Laminated Glass; Tempered Glass; Fire-Rated & Bullet-Resistant Glass
profile.themes: UAE Geopolitical Resilience; India Capacity Ramp-up; Product Mix Shift to High-Margin IG/Laminated

bull_bear.body: Debt reduction prioritized (repaid some promoter loans in Q4). Equity warrants (4 lakh) callable within 18 months, proceeds earmarked for potential second acquisition (currently under due diligence).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: UAE geopolitical instability impacting real estate demand or supply chains; slower-than-expected capacity utilization ramp-up in India (Glasstech units); raw material price volatility if pass-through mechanisms fail; execution risk on new product launches.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Highly optimistic and confident despite external headwinds; emphasizes 'genie in the bottle' regarding UAE resilience; transparent about integration teething issues in India; bullish on FY27 margin expansion to 18%.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: India revenue degrowth on a proforma basis (including pre-acquisition Glasstech) due to 2-quarter consolidation/re-engineering period and cessation of low-margin trading activities. Zero tax liability expected for next 2 years enhances cash flow. Saint-Gobain collaboration provides 4-5% price advantage and preferential order confirmation, not just marketing support.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body: UAE: Dominant revenue contributor (~60% of FY26), focused on high-margin IG and Laminated glass for facades. India: Transitioning from plain tempered (low margin) to IG/Laminated. Glasstech units (Taloja, Erode) reached EBITDA breakeven in March 2026; targeting 10%+ EBITDA margin in Q1 FY27. Silvassa unit operating at 17-18% EBITDA.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising energy costs and float glass prices squeezing fabricators without pricing power. | Sejal Glass Limited | beneficiary | High | Company explicitly stated ability to pass through 80-90% of raw material cost increases immediately due to make-to-order model and strong client relationships. |
| UAE real estate slowdown and geopolitical tension reducing demand for building materials. | Unorganized UAE Glass Fabricators | loser | Med | Sejal maintains AED 60mn order book and stable payments, suggesting market share consolidation towards organized players with strong balance sheets during turmoil. |
| Need for specialized high-safety glass (fire/bullet) in Indian infrastructure/railways. | Sejal Glass Limited | beneficiary | Med | First-mover advantage in India with new fire-rated tech from Spain and active bidding for Vande Bharat tenders, differentiating from commodity tempered glass competitors. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

latest_quarter.body: Raw material (float glass) prices up 7-8% due to energy surcharges; company passing through 80-90% of cost increases. Consolidated gross margin ~33-34% (UAE mix superior to India). India gross margin expansion expected as mix shifts from 60% plain tempered to high-value IG/Laminated, potentially lifting gross margin to 39-40% long-term.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: 25% base case (up to 40% if UAE stabilizes) for FY27; Target Topline >INR 500cr. Margin: 17.5%-18% EBITDA for FY27. Order Inflow: UAE maintaining AED 10.2-10.5mn/month; India Q1 FY27 expecting 20% QoQ growth. Capex/Commissioning: UAE expansion machines delayed by geopolitics, now scheduled for installation in Q2/Q3 FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Strong visibility in UAE with AED 60mn (~INR 135-140cr) order book; Q1 FY27 revenue visibility of AED 31mn, improving to AED 35mn in Q2. India order book growing via railway tenders (Vande Bharat) and commercial projects.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: New product lines (Fire-rated from Spain, Bullet-proof, Digital printed) launching Q3 FY26, targeting 5-7% revenue mix in FY26 and 15-20% in FY27. Railway segment entry (2-3% revenue contribution). Geographic diversification: Exports to Europe initiated from India; African market push from UAE.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Sejal Glass delivered a blowout Q4FY26 with 72% YoY revenue growth and 17.5% EBITDA margins, driven by UAE resilience and initial Glasstech integration. The core investment story pivots to FY27 where India operations (currently low utilization) must ramp to 50%+ to unlock consolidated 18% margin guidance, offsetting potential UAE volatility.
